newsitem.title: USA: Tribune sees strong EBITDA rise in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Tribune sees strong EBITDA rise in 1997.

text.p: Tribune Co said Friday it expects to show a strong rise in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) in 1997.

"We have great plans for the year ahead with the anticipated February closing of the $1 billion Renaissance acquisition," John Madigan, chairman, said in a statement. "Because of this and many other positive factors, 1997 should show another significant increase in EBITDA."
Tribune said in July 1996 it plans to acquire Renaissance Communications Corp, which owns six television stations.
For full-year 1996, consolidated EBITDA rose 20 percent to $633.0 million from $526.2 million. EBITDA also is before gains or losses on stock sales, Tribune said.

Earlier, it reported fourth quarter earnings or $0.63 a primary share, up from last year's $0.53 that included $0.06 in income from discontinued operations. For the year, it earned $2.88 a primary share, including $0.73 a share in discontinued operations income. In 1995, it earned $2.00 a primary share, including in $0.25 income from discontinued operations.
